I farm the way I know will keep the land steady and the work manageable for my household. I only have 7 mu, but I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for many years in Quzhou, so I will keep the full 7 mu in that system. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen to hold yield, and keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels because I want steady grain filling and stronger plants through winter and spring. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about reliable output on limited land, and I will fertilize a bit heavier on nitrogen than wheat because maize responds well and is my main summer yield driver. I will keep tillage simple with rotary work because my scale is small and I want practical field preparation without extra cost or labor. I will spray only as needed but still plan for basic disease, weed, and insect control. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to secure a solid harvest from both crops with work I can realistically manage at my age.
